---
title: "if and && long ignored everything but the first element"
ref: FLW-04
categories: [Control flow]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "an error, since the condition holds two values"
versions: "Silent up to R 4.1, an error for if since R 4.2.0, a warning then an error for && in R 4.2.0 and 4.3.0"
source: "The R Inferno, R 4.2.0 and 4.3.0 NEWS"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
x <- c(5, -1)
if (x > 0) {
  "all positive"
}

c(TRUE, FALSE) && TRUE
```
:::

Pick **R 4.1.3** in the menu, then run it again: the same code answers "all positive" with a mere warning, and `&&` returns `TRUE` without a word.

## Why

`if` expects a single logical value. Up to R 4.1, when given several, it used the first one and settled for a warning, easy to miss in a script or in a function called in a loop. Here, `x > 0` is `c(TRUE, FALSE)`: only the 5 was tested, the -1 went unnoticed.

`&&` and `||` were worse: they took the first element without any warning. R 4.2.0 turned the `if` case into an error and added a warning to `&&` and `||`, which became an error in R 4.3.0. An old script that "worked" can therefore stop dead after an R upgrade.

## The remedy

Say explicitly what you want to test across the whole vector.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
x <- c(5, -1)
if (all(x > 0)) {
  "all positive"
} else {
  "at least one value zero or negative"
}
any(x > 0)
```
:::
